summary.text: Case 1 is a patient aged 79 with arterial hypertension, obesity, coronary artery disease, heart failure and osteoporosis who was diagnosed with ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome. Baseline measurements included blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, BMI 30.4 kg/m^(2), morning cortisol 615 nmol/L and an overnight dexamethasone suppression test result of 598 nmol/L with no suppression. CT showed bilateral lipid-poor adrenal adenomas of 6x9 mm on the left and 16x17mm on the right.

Radical adrenalectomy was not considered suitable, so after two weeks of alpha-adrenergic blocker premedication the patient had computed tomography-guided microwave ablation in July, 2021, with the antenna in the right adrenal gland, at 30 W for 10 min under general anesthesia. Immediate post-procedure CT showed no enhancement of the targeted adenoma and no procedural complications were encountered, yet acute adrenal insufficiency with morning cortisol 225 nmol/L is listed as a post-treatment complication.

Follow-up at 1, 4, 10, 25 and 32 months recorded weight of 72, 70, 69, 68 and 65.8 kg, morning cortisol of 179, 135, 144, 363 and 371 nmol/L, and blood pressure of 140/80, 156/76, 186/105, 150/67 and 188/80 mmHg. The authors describe varying degrees of clinical improvement in all patients, and all patients continued antihypertensive therapy.

summary.text: Case 2 is a patient aged 52 with arterial hypertension, obesity, non-toxic multinodular goiter, insulin resistance and depression who was diagnosed with mild autonomous cortisol secretion. Baseline blood pressure was 170/100 mmHg, BMI 36.8 kg/m^(2), morning cortisol 317 nmol/L and the overnight dexamethasone suppression test result was 135 nmol/L with no suppression. CT showed a 7x11 mm right adrenal adenoma.

Radical adrenalectomy was not considered suitable, so after two weeks of alpha-adrenergic blocker premedication the patient had computed tomography-guided microwave ablation in September, 2023, with the antenna in the right adrenal gland, at 30 W in two 3-min cycles under general anesthesia. Immediate post-procedure CT showed no enhancement of the targeted adenoma, no procedural complications were encountered and the table lists no post-treatment complications.

Follow-up at 1, 4 and 11 months recorded weight of 104, 102 and 101 kg, blood pressure of 140/110, 117/78 and 128/80 mmHg, and overnight dexamethasone suppression test results of 47 nmol/L at 4 months and 46 nmol/L at 11 months. The authors describe varying degrees of clinical improvement in all patients, and all patients continued antihypertensive therapy.
